clue.text: Emails on mobile for pudding

indicators.note: mobile means moving about, so the letters of the words before it are free to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sends messages from a phone about what to have for dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Semolina boiled with milk and sugar is a classic British milk dessert, so it is a kind of pudding.

clue.text: Vegetable spread European put in bar

parts.note: butter is something spread on bread

indicators.note: put in tells us the European letter goes inside the word for bar

parts.note: to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: A European vegetable spread is being sold over a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: The butter bean is a large pale lima bean, a pulse eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Extremely attractive daughter in a position to get in

parts.words: in a position to get in
parts.note: a candidate able to win an election, to get in, is electable

explanation.surface: A very attractive daughter is well placed to be admitted somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get in' here means to win an election, not to enter a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Delectable means delightful or delicious, highly pleasing or attractive.

clue.text: Quarrel — it is bath time

parts.note: a spa is a place with mineral baths, and the city of Bath is itself a spa

explanation.surface: An argument breaks out over whose turn it is in the bath.
explanation.definitionFit: A spat is a short, petty argument, a minor quarrel or tiff.

clue.text: Old ruler cuts a regal show

indicators.note: show says the words before it display the answer inside them, running across the gaps

explanation.surface: A former monarch puts on a reduced royal display.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the emperor of Russia before 1917, so a monarch of the past.

clue.text: Outspoken lord's seaside attraction

indicators.note: outspoken here means spoken out loud, so we want a word sounding like the word for lord

parts.note: a peer is a member of the nobility, such as a lord

explanation.surface: A frank aristocrat owns a seaside amusement.
explanation.walkthrough: Outspoken looks like a description of the lord's manner; it signals a word that sounds the same as PEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A pier with arcades and rides is a typical attraction at a British seaside resort.

clue.text: Modest husband entering social class

indicators.note: entering says the husband's letter goes inside the word for social class

parts.note: a caste is a hereditary social class

explanation.surface: A demure husband marries into a higher social class.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure or restrained in behaviour, which is a sense of modest.

clue.text: Fast dog in cleric's office

indicators.note: in says the word for dog is placed inside the word for the cleric's office

parts.note: a see is a bishop's seat or diocese, a cleric's office
a cur is a mongrel dog

explanation.surface: A speedy dog has got into the vicar's office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast' looks like an adjective for the dog's speed; it means firmly fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Fast can mean firmly fixed or fastened, as in held fast, which is secure.

clue.text: Doctor hates pic, it's a copy

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are altered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor dislikes a picture because it is a fake.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastiche is a work imitating the style of another, a kind of copy.

clue.text: Snake beginning to tip vessel

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake

indicators.note: beginning to says take only the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A snake begins to tip a vessel over.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat is a small vessel for travelling on water.

clue.text: Plan to go in with lever

parts.note: to enter is to go in
to prise is to lever something open

explanation.surface: A scheme for getting inside using a crowbar.
explanation.definitionFit: An enterprise is a project or undertaking, a planned venture.

clue.text: Join Queen's row

parts.note: to tie is to join things together
R, for Regina, is a standard abbreviation for Queen

explanation.surface: Someone joins the Queen's line of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A tier is one of a series of rows placed one above another, as in theatre seating.

clue.text: Rush ass with, um, saccharin-sweet saga, say

parts.note: to tear is to rush along
a jerk is a fool, an ass
er and um are both hesitation sounds

explanation.surface: A foolish person hurries, stammering, through a sickly romantic story.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearjerker is a sentimental story, film or song designed to make people cry, of which a sugary saga is an example.

clue.text: Mail, eg, avoiding repetition produces lover

indicators.note: avoiding repetition says drop the letter that appears twice, keeping one

parts.note: chain mail is an example of armour

explanation.surface: Letters that avoid saying the same thing twice win someone a sweetheart.
explanation.walkthrough: ARMOUR contains R twice; dropping one R gives AMOUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour is a love affair, and by extension the person one loves, a lover.

clue.text: Something to get you down is guy on a run

parts.note: a guy is a rope used to secure a tent
a ladder is a run in a stocking or tights

explanation.surface: A depressing man is out jogging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get you down' suggests something depressing; it means to help you climb down.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladder made of rope is used to climb down from a height, such as a ship's side.

clue.text: Valley could be described by German beer

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for German, from Deutsch
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A valley could be summed up by a German beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A dale is a valley, especially in northern England.

clue.text: Bishop's office, eg, swept by this

parts.note: B is the chess notation for a bishop
an office is an example of a room

explanation.surface: A bishop's office is swept clean with a brush.
explanation.definitionFit: A broom is a long-handled brush used for sweeping floors.

clue.text: Is getting into duck a nuisance?

indicators.note: getting into says the letter for is goes inside the word for duck

parts.note: duck is a British term of endearment, like pet
is shortens to 's, as in it's

explanation.surface: A pond bird turns out to be an annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' is not the bird but the northern English endearment, as in 'thanks, duck'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pest is an annoying person or thing, a nuisance.

clue.text: Are fares are out of order for Sinbad?

indicators.note: out of order says these letters must be put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Sinbad's prices are wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinbad the Sailor of the Arabian Nights is an example of one who travels by sea.

clue.text: Oscar to write arcana which everyone knows

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to pen is to write
arcana are mysteries or secrets

explanation.surface: Oscar Wilde sets out to write about hidden mysteries.
explanation.definitionFit: An open secret is something supposed to be confidential but known by all.

clue.text: Promote pawn to point

parts.note: P is the chess abbreviation for pawn
to refer someone to something is to point them to it

explanation.surface: A chess player promotes a pawn by advancing it to a square.
explanation.definitionFit: To prefer someone is an old sense meaning to advance them in rank, to promote.

clue.text: Church windows include this in the first place

definitions.meaning: stained-glass windows have their pieces held in strips of a soft grey metal
to be in front, first in a race, is to be in this position

explanation.definitionFit: Lead is the metal in leaded windows, and being in the lead means being first.

clue.text: Free chat with healer is what's given by doctor

indicators.note: free means released from its fixed form, so these letters are set loose and reordered

parts.note: taken as written
with is a link and healer is taken as written

explanation.surface: A friendly chat with a healer costs nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Healthcare is the medical care and treatment that a doctor provides.

clue.text: Clout a source of illumination

definitions.meaning: to clout is to hit hard, and to ... someone is British slang for punching them

explanation.definitionFit: Lamp is a light, and as a British slang verb it means to hit someone.

clue.text: Search out knight in shed

indicators.note: in says the knight's letter goes inside the word for shed

parts.note: a hut is a small shed
N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: Someone is looking for a knight hiding in a shed.
explanation.definitionFit: To hunt is to search for something or someone in order to find it.

clue.text: Lop the top off Jeeves' bloody friend

indicators.note: lop the top off says drop the first letter of the word that follows

parts.note: bally is a mild euphemism for bloody, used in the world of Wodehouse's Jeeves and Wooster

explanation.surface: A butler's violent friend has his head cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: Bertie Wooster, Jeeves's master in P G Wodehouse's comic novels, says 'bally' where others would say 'bloody'.
explanation.definitionFit: An ally is a supporter or associate, a friend.

clue.text: Newspaper on duke, otherwise a pain

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means the newspaper comes after the duke

parts.note: rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A newspaper reports on a duke, who is otherwise a bore.
explanation.definitionFit: A drag is a tedious or annoying thing, a bore or a pain.

clue.text: Where tramline starts?

parts.note: a tram route begins and ends at a station, and the word for it is also made of the letters of tramline

explanation.definitionFit: A terminal is the station at either end of a transport route, where a line begins.

clue.text: Some fun eventually is rough

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Fun that only arrives late is hard going.
explanation.definitionFit: An uneven surface is bumpy, which is what rough means of ground.
